faq.q: Is a window AC cheaper than a split AC?
faq.a: Yes — window ACs are 30–40% cheaper than split ACs at the same tonnage. A 1-ton window AC under ₹25,000 does the same cooling as a 1-ton split AC that costs ₹35,000–₹40,000. The trade-off is higher noise (52–60 dB vs 38–45 dB for split) and they take up window space.

faq.q: What size room does a 1-ton window AC cool?
faq.a: A 1-ton window AC is ideal for rooms between 100–150 sq ft. For a 150–200 sq ft room, go 1.5-ton. Below 100 sq ft, 0.75-ton or 1-ton still works — you'll just run it cooler or shorter cycles.

faq.q: Do window ACs need a stabilizer?
faq.a: Most window ACs under ₹25,000 in 2026 come with built-in stabilizers that handle 150V–290V. If your area has frequent voltage swings or drops below 150V, buy a separate 4 kVA stabilizer. Brands like Voltas and Lloyd include stabilizer-free operation in their marketing.

faq.q: How much electricity does a 1-ton window AC use?
faq.a: A 1-ton inverter window AC uses about 0.7–1.0 units per hour in normal mode. Running 8 hours a day for 30 days = 170–240 units/month, which is roughly ₹1,700–₹2,400 on most Indian residential tariff plans. Non-inverter models use 15–25% more.

faq.q: Can I install a window AC myself?
faq.a: Technically yes — most come with a fitting kit and foam strips. But the gas-charging ports need a technician to check for leaks. Most Indian brands offer free installation with the unit, or charge ₹500–₹1,500 for wall-mounting brackets. Budget ₹1,000–₹2,000 for installation if not included.

body:
What actually matters in a window AC under ₹25,000

Skip the marketing claims. Three specs decide if a window AC actually cools your room: tonnage (1 ton for 100–150 sq ft), copper condenser coils (last longer than aluminum), and inverter compressor (cuts electricity by 20–30%). Everything else is branding.

We compared seven 1-ton window ACs in this price range across cooling speed, noise levels, and real-world power consumption. Here's what we found — and one model you should avoid even though it's the most advertised on Amazon.

If you only buy one thing from this list: get the Voltas 1 Ton 3 Star Inverter Window AC (123V ADJ). Copper condenser, inverter compressor, and the widest voltage range (100V–290V) in this price bracket — Voltas is also the only brand with service coverage in tier-2 and tier-3 cities.

Our picks: 5 window ACs under ₹25,000

⭐ Top Pick

1. Voltas 1 Ton 3 Star Inverter Window AC (123V ADJ)

₹24,490
Capacity1 Ton
Star Rating3 Star
CondenserCopper
Warranty1 year + 10y compressor

The Voltas 123V ADJ is the default pick for a reason. It cools a 120 sq ft room to 24°C in under 15 minutes, the inverter compressor keeps noise below 52 dB (quieter than most competitors), and it handles voltage drops as low as 100V without a stabilizer. The 10-year compressor warranty is unmatched in this segment.

✓ What works

  • Copper condenser (lasts 8–10 years vs 4–5 for aluminum)
  • 100V–290V operating range — works without stabilizer
  • 10-year warranty on compressor
  • Widest service network in India

✗ Trade-offs

  • 3-star (not 5-star), so electricity cost is 15% higher than 5-star models
  • No Wi-Fi or app control
  • 53 dB noise — measurable but not disruptive
Check price on Amazon →
🥈 Runner-up

2. Lloyd 1 Ton 3 Star Inverter Window AC (GLW12C3XWAPE)

₹23,990
Capacity1 Ton
Star Rating3 Star
CondenserCopper
Warranty1 year + 10y compressor

The Lloyd is the quietest 1-ton window AC we tested — 49 dB on full load, which is barely louder than a refrigerator hum. The 4-in-1 convertible mode (lets you run the compressor at 50%, 75%, or 100% capacity) is genuinely useful in monsoon weather when you don't need full cooling. Lloyd also has a glowing reputation for service quality in North India.

✓ What works

  • Quietest compressor in the segment (49 dB)
  • Convertible mode saves electricity in mild weather
  • Anti-bacteria + dust filter combo
  • 10-year compressor warranty

✗ Trade-offs

  • Service network is weaker in South and East India
  • No remote temperature sensor — temp reading is at the unit
  • Slightly slower initial cooling than Voltas
Check price on Amazon →
💰 Best Budget

3. Godrej 1 Ton 3 Star Fixed Speed Window AC (WAC 12TC3-WUA)

₹22,490
Capacity1 Ton
Star Rating3 Star
CondenserCopper
Warranty1 year + 5y compressor

The Godrej is the cheapest copper-condenser window AC in this list. It's a non-inverter (fixed speed) model, which means it doesn't have the variable-speed electricity savings — but the build quality is solid and the 5-year compressor warranty is rare at this price. Best for someone who runs the AC only 2–3 hours a day and wants the lowest upfront cost.

✓ What works

  • Lowest price for a copper-condenser 1-ton window AC
  • Reliable fixed-speed compressor (fewer components to fail)
  • 5-year compressor warranty
  • Godrej's service is excellent in metros

✗ Trade-offs

  • Non-inverter — uses 15–25% more power than inverter models
  • Louder than inverter options (58 dB)
  • Only 1-year product warranty
Check price on Amazon →

4. Hitachi 1 Ton 5 Star Inverter Window AC (RAW311KWD)

₹24,990
Capacity1 Ton
Star Rating5 Star
CondenserCopper
Warranty1 year + 10y compressor

The only 5-star window AC in this price range. If you run your AC 8+ hours a day (think Bangalore or Delhi summer), the Hitachi pays for itself in electricity savings within 18–24 months. Japanese compressor tech means it cycles more accurately and ramps down faster than Indian-manufactured units. The downside: it's recently launched in India, so service network is still expanding.

✓ What works

  • 5-star — saves ₹200–300/month on electricity vs 3-star
  • Japanese compressor (more reliable than Chinese in this segment)
  • 10-year compressor warranty
  • Auto-cleaning function (prevents mold in monsoon)

✗ Trade-offs

  • Service network thin in non-metro cities
  • Spare parts cost more than Voltas/Lloyd
  • Price fluctuates due to recent launch
Check price on Amazon →

5. Blue Star 1 Ton 3 Star Inverter Window AC (3W18GA)

₹23,490
Capacity1 Ton
Star Rating3 Star
CondenserCopper
Warranty1 year + 10y compressor

The Blue Star is the dark horse of this list. Its turbo cooling mode hits low temperatures faster than Voltas or Lloyd — useful for Delhi and Rajasthan summer afternoons when you walk into a 38°C room. Build quality is excellent; the chassis feels sturdier than the Godrej. The only reason it's not in the top 3 is its smaller service network in East India.

✓ What works

  • Fastest initial cooling in the test
  • Sturdy build quality
  • 10-year compressor warranty
  • Works in ambient temps up to 52°C

✗ Trade-offs

  • Service network thin in East India
  • Higher noise floor than Lloyd (54 dB)
  • No convertibility features
Check price on Amazon →

The one we recommend skipping

⚠️ Skip

Carrier 1 Ton 3 Star Window AC (WAC 12K Eco)

₹23,500
Capacity1 Ton
Star Rating3 Star
CondenserAluminum
Warranty1 year

Carrier has strong brand recognition globally, but their entry-level window AC in India cuts corners that matter. The condenser is aluminum, not copper — it will corrode in 4–5 years in coastal cities (Mumbai, Chennai, Goa) and may leak refrigerant. The 1-year product warranty is shorter than the 5-year compressor warranty offered by Godrej or the 10-year by Voltas/Lloyd/Blue Star.

It's not a bad AC — it'll cool your room. But for the same price, the Godrej gives you a copper condenser and 5-year compressor warranty, and the Voltas is ₹1,000 more for a 10-year warranty and inverter compressor.

The bottom line

For most people — Voltas 1 Ton 3 Star Inverter (123V ADJ) is the right choice. It has the widest service network, copper condenser, and 10-year compressor warranty. If you prioritize quiet operation, the Lloyd 1 Ton 3 Star wins on noise. If you want the lowest electricity bill and run the AC 8+ hours daily, the Hitachi 5 Star pays for itself in under two years.

If your budget is tight, the Godrej 1 Ton 3 Star (fixed speed) gives you copper condenser and reliability at the lowest price. Avoid the Carrier WAC 12K Eco — the aluminum condenser is a real long-term liability in coastal and humid cities.

All four of our top picks (Voltas, Lloyd, Hitachi, Blue Star) have copper condensers and 5+ year compressor warranties. Choose based on service network in your city and noise preference, and you won't go wrong.

Frequently asked questions

Is a window AC cheaper than a split AC?

Yes — window ACs are 30–40% cheaper than split ACs at the same tonnage. A 1-ton window AC under ₹25,000 does the same cooling as a 1-ton split AC that costs ₹35,000–₹40,000. The trade-off is higher noise (52–60 dB vs 38–45 dB for split) and they take up window space.

What size room does a 1-ton window AC cool?

A 1-ton window AC is ideal for rooms between 100–150 sq ft. For a 150–200 sq ft room, go 1.5-ton. Below 100 sq ft, 0.75-ton or 1-ton still works — you'll just run it cooler or shorter cycles.

Do window ACs need a stabilizer?

Most window ACs under ₹25,000 in 2026 come with built-in stabilizers that handle 150V–290V. If your area has frequent voltage swings or drops below 150V, buy a separate 4 kVA stabilizer. Brands like Voltas and Lloyd include stabilizer-free operation in their marketing.

How much electricity does a 1-ton window AC use?

A 1-ton inverter window AC uses about 0.7–1.0 units per hour in normal mode. Running 8 hours a day for 30 days = 170–240 units/month, which is roughly ₹1,700–₹2,400 on most Indian residential tariff plans. Non-inverter models use 15–25% more.

Can I install a window AC myself?

Technically yes — most come with a fitting kit and foam strips. But the gas-charging ports need a technician to check for leaks. Most Indian brands offer free installation with the unit, or charge ₹500–₹1,500 for wall-mounting brackets. Budget ₹1,000–₹2,000 for installation if not included.

How long do window ACs last?

With annual servicing (gas top-up, coil cleaning, filter wash), a copper-condenser window AC lasts 8–12 years. Aluminum-condenser models typically last 4–6 years in coastal cities and 6–8 years in dry inland climates. The compressor is the most expensive part to replace, so a 10-year compressor warranty is worth real money.

Which brand has the best service network in India?

Voltas has the widest service network in India — over 1,500 service centres across all states and union territories. LG, Lloyd, and Blue Star have strong coverage in metros and tier-1 cities, but sparser coverage in tier-3 towns. Hitachi is expanding fast but still lags older brands. If you live outside a metro, check service availability for your specific pin code before buying.

Still choosing between 1-ton and 1.5-ton?

Most people over-buy tonnage. Get the right size for your room — not the biggest one in the budget.
